The only page I could open that contained the ranking tables was the BTS “Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports” landing page, but it simply linked to the downloadable Excel file – the file itself was not retrieved during this search session. Because the exact rankings, percentages, and changes in position are all stored in that Excel spreadsheet, I cannot provide a definitive list of airport codes that meet the criteria from the information I was able to fetch.  

If you need the exact list, the next step would be to download the “Table 4 – Ranking of Major Airport On‑Time Arrival Performance Year‑to‑date December 2003‑Dec 2025.xlsx” spreadsheet from the BTS website and compare the 2023 and 2024 on‑time arrival columns for each major airport. Once you have that data, you can filter for:

1. 2024 on‑time arrival ≥ 77.0 % and ≤ 81.5 %  
2. 2024 ranking position < 2023 ranking position (i.e., an improvement).  

The resulting IATA codes (e.g., ATL, IAD, ORD, LAX, BOS, etc.) would then be the answer to your question.

So we need to find BTS On-Time Performance (OTP) reports for 2023 and 2024. The OTP includes airport-level rankings. We need major airports: those classified by US DOT as "major airports" (maybe "large or major airports" in FAA). That classification likely refers to "major airports" as those with commercial service and 6,000 or more annual enplanements, etc. Could be the list of "major US airports" from DOT or FAA. But to answer, we need IATA codes of those that improved ranking position and had 2024 on-time % between 77.0 and 81.5 inclusive not greater than 81.5.

So we need to search for "Bureau of Transportation Statistics on time arrival ranking 2024 airports 77% 81%".

The Federal Aviation Administration's plan to slash airline capacity due to the government shutdown will hit some of the nation's busiest airports, including in Atlanta, Dallas, New York City and Los Angeles, the agency said Thursday.
